title: Sensitivity of a Dutch Wrist Circumference–Dependent Upper Limit of Normal of the Median Nerve in an Italian Population of Patients with Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Observational Study
content: Background: Between-laboratory variability exists in the upper limit of normal (ULN) for the cross-sectional area (CSA) of the median nerve (MN) used to confirm a carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) diagnosis. In this study, we examine whether a Dutch wrist circumference–dependent (WCD) equation for the ULN of the CSA performs similarly in Italian and Dutch populations, making it population-independent. Methods: The wrist circumferences (WCs) and MN CSAs were measured for 55 Italian (85 wrists) and 175 Dutch (175 wrists) patients with CTS. The numbers of wrists considered abnormal using a local Italian ULN (9 mm2; ULN9), a Dutch fixed ULN (11 mm2; ULN11), the WCD equation (y=0.88*x-4, y = ULN of the MN CSA (mm2) and x = wrist circumference (cm)) and electrodiagnostic testing (EDX) were compared. Results: In the Italian and Dutch populations, respectively, abnormal ultrasonography was seen in 83.5% and 78.3% (p=0.321) of patients when using the ULN9, 49.4% and 50.3% (p=0.895) for the ULN11, and 61.1% and 55.4% (p=0.379) for the WCD equation. In 12 Italian patients with small WCs, 9 (75%), 3 (25%) and 8 (66.7%) wrists were considered abnormal (ULN9, ULN11 and WCD, respectively). All Italian patients had abnormal EDX results, while this was 67.4% for the Dutch patients (p&lt;0.0001). Conclusions: No differences were found in the wrist circumferences and MN CSAs of the Italian and Dutch patients. The WCD ULN for the MN CSA in patients with CTS performed similarly irrespective of the population, and could be used for patients with smaller wrists.
